clue.text: Eventual outcome of a highly successful play

definitions.meaning: what happens 'in the ...', over the course of time, is the eventual result
a hit show stays on stage for many months of performances

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both the extended stretch of time over which things settle and a show's lengthy stay in a theatre.

clue.text: Bubbly set without the right to be so

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round the others

parts.note: to lay something is to set it down, as in laying a table

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a bubbly drinks set lacks the proper licence to be fizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: LAY goes round THE plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: Something covered in froth or foam, like soapsuds, is bubbly.

clue.text: An AIF supplied comforts for the troops

indicators.note: the letters are supplied in a different arrangement, so they are reworked

explanation.surface: The Australian Imperial Force provided home comforts to its soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: AIF is the Australian Imperial Force, a red herring. The NAAFI (Navy, Army and Air Force Institutes) runs canteens and shops for British forces.
explanation.definitionFit: The forces' canteen organisation supplies servicemen with food, drink and small luxuries.

clue.text: Exercises a certain sense in actual practice

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, as the word in places it

parts.note: something actual is real
someone who hears is using the sense of hearing

explanation.surface: A trainee puts one of the senses to work during real-life practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-through before a performance is a practice session.

clue.text: Plutocrat heard turning down Robert's request

indicators.note: signals that the words are taken as spoken, matching a word with another spelling

parts.note: refusing Bob would be saying 'Nah, Bob'

explanation.surface: A rich man is overheard refusing what Robert asked for.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob is short for Robert; a casual refusal to him sounds like the word for a wealthy grandee.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob is a person of great wealth, originally one who made a fortune in India, so a plutocrat.

clue.text: Baby's father first supported nihilistic art movement

parts.note: a baby calls its father dada
written as 1st, read with the figure as the letter I

explanation.surface: An infant's dad, an early backer, championed an anti-art movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is 1ST with the 1 read as I. The early twentieth-century Dada movement rejected conventional art.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Dada belonged to the deliberately absurd, anti-establishment art movement.

clue.text: Disk Ernie manufactured for an engraver

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: ERNIE, the premium bond machine, had a disk made by an engraver.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE is the computer that picks British Premium Bond winners.
explanation.definitionFit: A die-sinker cuts the dies used to stamp coins and medals, a kind of engraver.

clue.text: Duck stratagem

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to duck is to evade or sidestep
a trick or ruse to get round something

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to evade by moving aside and a crafty trick.

clue.text: Showmen make mark endlessly with air-conditioning

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter, so it has no end

parts.note: to impress is to make a mark on something

indicators.note: the letters are conditioned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Showmen keep making an impression with air-conditioned venues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last S of IMPRESS; 'conditioning' rearranges AIR to ARI.
explanation.definitionFit: Impresarios are theatrical producers and promoters, the people behind the show.

clue.text: We hear it's the magazine for gossip

indicators.note: signals that a word is taken as spoken, matching one with another spelling

parts.note: Tatler is a British society magazine

explanation.surface: Word is that this magazine is the one for gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: Tatler is a long-running British glossy covering high society.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattler is someone who chatters and tells tales, a gossip.

clue.text: Everyone included in list is educable

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a table is a list of figures or names
each means every one taken individually

explanation.surface: Everyone on the register is capable of being taught.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone educable is able to learn, so able to be taught.

clue.text: Last place to expect public transport to go to

definitions.text: Last place to expect public transport to go to

parts.words: Last place to expect public transport to go to
parts.note: reads like 'nowhere buses ever go', but buses end their day by heading back to the garage

explanation.definitionFit: Buses and trains finish their runs at the garage or yard where they are kept.

clue.text: I laze about and do little, from the sound of it

definitions.text: do little, from the sound of it
definitions.note: Doolittle is the surname, sounding like 'do little'

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A lazy person lounges around and does next to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliza Doolittle is the flower girl in Shaw's Pygmalion and My Fair Lady; the definition hints at her surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's heroine's surname sounds like the phrase, so her first name completes it.

clue.text: Newly-wed hale and hearty in prison

parts.note: a bride has just married
someone in good health is well

explanation.surface: A healthy bride finds herself in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridewell was a London house of correction whose name came to mean any prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of an old London jail became a general word for a lock-up.

clue.text: Benchmark which is to the credit of detectives

parts.note: the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters, so belonging to detectives is Yard's
on tick means on credit

explanation.surface: Something counts in the police's favour.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is London's Metropolitan Police headquarters; 'tick' is British slang for credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard used to measure or judge things is a benchmark.

clue.text: Programmes of course for ethnic identity

definitions.meaning: printed lists of runners at a racecourse
taken as cards showing one's race

explanation.definitionFit: These are racegoers' printed guides to the day's runners, and whimsically documents stating ethnicity.

clue.text: Performing together

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means playing live before an audience and also acting in agreement.

clue.text: I fish out it to sit on

indicators.note: one piece sits out round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: the char is a fish of the trout family

explanation.surface: Someone fishes out a seat for a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' means outside here: CHAR goes round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair is a seat, furniture made for sitting.

clue.text: Indicate where many deposit first in a hole in the wall

indicators.note: tells us this piece comes at the front

parts.note: cash is what many people put into a bank
to point is to indicate

explanation.surface: Show where people put their savings first, at a hole in the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hole in the wall' is British slang for a cash machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash machine set into a bank's outside wall is nicknamed a hole in the wall.

clue.text: Double about about about a duke

indicators.note: one piece goes about, surrounding, the other

parts.note: dual means double
C stands for circa, about

explanation.surface: A stammering report about a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: The three 'about's do different jobs: C (circa), the container signal, and 'concerning' in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducal means relating to a duke or dukedom.

clue.text: Hurt old mother first

indicators.note: tells us this piece comes at the front

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
aged means old

explanation.surface: The elderly were hurt and mothers came first.
explanation.definitionFit: Something damaged has been harmed or injured.

clue.text: Fletcher, a man of the church

definitions.meaning: Fletcher ... led the mutiny on the Bounty

explanation.definitionFit: Fletcher's surname, and a follower of Christ.

clue.text: So-called lion-man running wild

indicators.note: the letters run out of control into a new order

explanation.surface: A supposed half-lion, half-man creature is on the loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Nominal means in name only, as so-called suggests.

clue.text: Garbled verse about finishing off pasta

indicators.note: this piece comes at the end of the other

parts.note: macaroni is a tube-shaped pasta
C stands for circa, about

explanation.surface: Muddled poetry is written about polishing off a plate of pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: Macaronic verse mixes languages, often Latin and the vernacular, for comic effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry jumbling two languages is called macaronic, from a mock-Latin poem about macaroni.

clue.text: Author produces most of the book

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a reader is a school reading book

explanation.surface: A writer turns out the bulk of a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, author of The Cloister and the Hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, an author.

clue.text: It may go by ship and go by car

indicators.note: one piece goes beside the other

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Freight may travel by sea or by road.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods carried on a ship are its freight.

clue.text: Introduction Rex put into verse

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a poem is a piece of verse
R stands for Rex, king

explanation.surface: A king wrote a preface in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A proem is a preface or preamble to a book or speech.

clue.text: He recorded a hit in Hamlet'

definitions.text: He recorded a hit in Hamlet

parts.words: He recorded a hit in Hamlet
parts.note: sounds like a pop star, but refers to the courtier who judges the fencing match in Shakespeare's play and calls 'a hit, a very palpable hit'

explanation.definitionFit: The foppish courtier in Hamlet umpires the duel and records each hit.

clue.text: A drawback for the Irish police

indicators.note: the word drawback splits so back tells us to read the letters backwards

parts.note: to drag is to draw along

explanation.surface: There is a disadvantage for Ireland's police force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawback' splits into DRAW, giving DRAG, and BACK, the reversal signal on A DRAG.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garda Síochána is the national police force of Ireland.

clue.text: Prior or noble I put the Queen on to

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A prior or a noble has the Queen added to his rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier on means at a previous time, before.

clue.text: Drop of French perfume

parts.note: de is French for of
scent is perfume

explanation.surface: Someone dabs a drop of French perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: A descent is a fall or downward slope, a drop.

clue.text: Visual changes to the Capitol

indicators.note: the letters undergo changes into a new order

explanation.surface: The appearance of the Capitol building has been altered.
explanation.walkthrough: The Capitol is the US Congress building in Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical means relating to sight, so visual.
